topics.topic: EXIF date-time full-match and calendar-validity requirements
questions: Must a raw `DateTimeOriginal` or `DateTime` value match this pattern in full, and must the matched components also form a valid calendar date and time?
Must the entire camera value match this pattern, and are leading or trailing characters or whitespace forbidden without normalization?
Is a value that matches `EXIF_DATETIME_PATTERN` but is not a real calendar date or time malformed, and must it be skipped rather than fail the placement or be normalized?
Must both `DateTimeOriginal` and `DateTime` match this pattern in full, and is a nonmatching value what A2 calls malformed?

quotes: _parse_exif_moment: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST return None unless text, once its trailing NUL characters and spaces are removed, matches the pattern of the imported EXIF_DATETIME_PATTERN constant whole and is a valid calendar date and time; that local time MUST be read at the offset _camera_offset gives for offset, or, when it gives None, in zone taking the first occurrence of a time that occurs twice and the offset in force before the change for a time that does not exist, and turned into UTC by _to_naive_utc; it MUST return None when the UTC year is before the imported CAMERA_EARLIEST_YEAR constant or the moment lies more than the imported CAMERA_LATEST_AFTER_MODIFIED_HOURS constant of hours after modified, and the moment otherwise.
judgement.why: The State 7 note requires a whole match after the stated trailing-character normalization, requires a valid calendar date and time, and rejects invalid values by returning None.

questions: Which authority supplies `marked_at`, at what event is it read, is it represented as naive UTC or offset-aware time, and how many clock readings may a new or replayed mark operation take?
What authority supplies the fresh instant written to `marked_at` when a publication mark is first created?
In what representation and time zone is `marked_at` stored and returned?
How many clock readings does a mark operation take when it creates the mark, and how many does a replay or conflicting mark take?

judgement.why: P2 judged the same clock authority, representation, sampling point and read-count question, and neither A7 nor the quoted model passages changed.

precedent.topic: Clock, representation, and read-count semantics for PublicationMark.marked_at
quotes:
1. The system clock is the one source of the current time, declared as `rules.time_source_policy`
   and reaching code through `system_clock_backend` as the operation `utc_now`.

2. Only a mark reads it, once, after the token, the request form and the identifiers are accepted and
   before the connection is examined or the project lock is taken. A mark refused before that point does
   not read it. A mark refused after it, and a replayed mark, have read it and write nothing. Scan, delivery
   and the health answer never read it.

3. The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no
   rounding, written in ISO 8601 form as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, followed by `.` and six digits when
   the microseconds are not zero, with no offset. Every instant of a record and an answer is written
   so. It sets `marked_at`.

- INV-13: a counting clock is read once by a mark and not at all by a scan, a delivery or the health answer (`test_only_the_mark_reads_the_clock`), and `marked_at` equals that reading (`test_a_marked_photo_is_reported_as_published`).
precedent.why: The clock source, representation, reading point and Required tests passage are unchanged from the closed State 2, and the credential/environment-setting changes did not make this topic matter.

topics.topic: Single file modification-time reading reused for plausibility and fallback
questions: Must one placement read the file's modification time exactly once and use that same instant both for camera-time plausibility and as the fallback photo moment?
How many times may one placement read the file modification time, and must the same captured instant be used both for camera-time plausibility and as the fallback photo moment?

judgement.why: P10 judged the same question about capturing one modification instant and reusing it for A2's plausibility comparison and fallback, and the relevant passages are unchanged.

precedent.topic: Whether the file modification instant is captured once and reused for photo-time decisions
quotes:
A file that is read takes its modification time from one metadata reading of the file that was
opened, the one whose bytes are read, taken after the opening and before the read; A7 rule 4 gives its
form, and a delivery uses that time under A2 rule 3.
precedent.why: The text requires one metadata reading of the opened file and requires delivery, including A2's comparison and fallback, to use that time.

topics.topic: File modification-time precision and timezone representation
questions: When the filesystem modification instant has sub-second precision, must that precision be preserved, rounded, or truncated in `taken_at` and `photo_date`, and is the resulting UTC datetime naive or offset-aware before delivery?

quotes:
3. The current time is a `datetime` in UTC without an offset, with microsecond precision and no
   rounding, written in ISO 8601 form as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, followed by `.` and six digits when
   the microseconds are not zero, with no offset. Every instant of a record and an answer is written
   so. It sets `marked_at`.

4. A file's modification time is converted to the same form before it is compared or delivered, dropping
   any fraction finer than a microsecond toward the earlier instant.
judgement.why: The modification instant is converted to naive UTC at microsecond precision, preserving microseconds and truncating only finer fractions toward the earlier instant.

topics.topic: STOP_SIGNALS member representation and operating-system signal resolution
questions: Are the tuple members literal signal-name strings, and, if so, exactly how are they resolved to and compared with the operating system's signal identifiers?

quotes:
included; SERVED, value `served`: after it, a signal of the imported `STOP_SIGNALS` constant stops the web server, which returns without
an error, and nothing fails until the process ends; and SERVER_FAILED, value `server_failed`: after it, the
process ends in any other way, a failure during or after the shutdown of a stopped server included, so any
failure after the boundary outranks the signal.
judgement.why: The table makes the members string names and the exit rule requires signals named by that constant to produce the SERVED path when shutdown succeeds; the internal name-to-operating-system resolution mechanism may vary but may not change that prescribed outcome.
